proposition: Ibn Turka had three sons and seven daughters on MK's inference from Yazdī's letter to Afżal al-Dīn Turka, which fits his own statement in the second Nafsat that he had ten children and a few wives; after his death (ca. 835/1432?) his son Ḥabīb Allāh Turka quarrelled with his brothers over money and Yazdī housed him.

mediation.who: Sharaf al-Dīn Yazdī, to Afżal al-Dīn Muḥammad Turka
mediation.note: A business letter, not about Ibn Turka's own doctrines.

mediation.who: Melvin-Koushki, summarising, dating and identifying the letter(s)
